text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

The panel's composition is not evidence. Women are heavily represented in planning, HR and local-government management, so all-women panels occur frequently by chance alone — inferring bias from it is the same reasoning you'd reject if applied to you.

Your credentials look stronger on paper, but director roles are rarely won on credentials. They turn on political judgement, council relations, conflict management and public-facing composure — exactly what "extensive public consultation experience" signals. Two interviews means the decision was made in the room, not on the CV.

Raising the panel's sex would read as sour grapes and damage your reputation in a small professional world. Instead, chase the written feedback in writing, politely, and ask what would make you competitive next time.
